stem: Chipo will plant 2.4 ha of maize near Marondera at 80 cm × 25 cm. She sows two seeds per station and thins to one plant. Assume each seed has a mass of 0.3 g.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the plant population per hectare after thinning.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the mass of seed, in kg, she needs for the whole field.
parts.explanation: Stations = 50,000 × 2.4 = 120,000; seeds = 240,000; × 0.3 g = 72,000 g = 72 kg. Forgetting the second seed gives 36 kg; giving the rate per hectare only gives 30 kg.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Stations = 50,000 × 2.4 = 120,000; seeds = 240,000; × 0.3 g = 72,000 g = 72 kg. Forgetting the second seed gives 36 kg; giving the rate per hectare only gives 30 kg.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Why does Chipo thin the seedlings to one plant per station?

options.content: To avoid competition so each plant forms a good cob
To let the removed seedlings be transplanted to another field
To raise the plant population per hectare
options.rationale: Thinning lowers the number of plants.

options.content: To make the plants flower and tassel much earlier
options.rationale: Thinning is not done to change flowering.

parts.explanation: Two plants at one station compete for water, nutrients and light.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Name the pest whose larvae cause dead hearts and tunnels in maize stems.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain why hybrid maize seed must be bought every season.

points.description: Hybrid seed is F1 from crossing two inbred lines, uniform with hybrid vigour.
Saved seed (F2) gives variable plants and lower yields.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: State **two** factors Chipo should consider when choosing a maize cultivar.

points.description: Maturity group to suit the natural region / length of season / planting date.
Disease resistance (e.g. maize streak virus, grey leaf spot) / yield potential / market or grain type.

explanation: Plant population, seed requirement and cultivar choice for maize.
hints: Plants/ha = 10,000 ÷ (row spacing × in-row spacing in m).

stem:
Tendai has 14 ha of arable land divided into four equal fields. He follows a four-course rotation in the order maize → groundnuts → sunflower → grass ley, moving each crop one field along every year.

| Field | Year 1 crop |
| --- | --- |
| A | Maize (receives manure) |
| B | Groundnuts |
| C | Sunflower |
| D | Grass ley |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which crop will grow in field A in year 2?

options.rationale: Maize moves to the field that had the ley.

parts.explanation: Field A had maize in year 1, so it carries groundnuts in year 2.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the area of each field, in ha.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Name the plant family (group) to which groundnuts belong.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Manure is applied at 12 t/ha to the maize course only. Calculate the mass of manure needed each year, in tonnes.
parts.explanation: 12 × 3.5 = 42 t. Applying it to all 14 ha would need 168 t.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 12 × 3.5 = 42 t. Applying it to all 14 ha would need 168 t.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain why maize is followed by groundnuts.

points.description: Maize is a heavy feeder that removes much nitrogen; groundnuts fix their own nitrogen through Rhizobium.
Groundnuts are a different family, so maize pests, diseases and witchweed have no host.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Explain **three** advantages of including the grass ley in the rotation.

points.description: Rests the soil and builds up organic matter from dense grass roots.
Improves soil structure and protects the soil from erosion.
Provides grazing or hay; manure from grazing animals improves fertility for the next maize.

explanation: Follow, calculate and justify a four-course rotation.
hints: Field A grows the next crop in the order.
Only the maize course gets manure.

stem:
A diagram of an ox-drawn mouldboard plough is described by its labelled parts.

| Label | Description |
| --- | --- |
| P | Pointed steel blade at the bottom front of the body |
| Q | Curved plate behind P |
| R | Flat plate on the side opposite Q |
| S | Metal piece at the front of the beam with holes in two rows |
| T | Small wheel under the front of the beam |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Match each labelled part with its function.

right.content: Presses on the furrow wall to keep the plough straight
Hitch used to adjust depth and width of cut
Lifts and turns the furrow slice over

parts.explanation: P share, Q mouldboard, R landside, S hake.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: What happens if part T is raised?

options.rationale: Lowering the wheel makes it shallower.
Correct: the share runs lower relative to the wheel.

options.content: The mouldboard stops turning the soil
options.rationale: The mouldboard still turns the slice.

parts.explanation: Raising the wheel lets the body go deeper.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Describe how the plough should be maintained at the end of the ploughing season.

points.description: Clean off all soil and repair or replace worn parts (share, heel) and loose bolts.
Coat bright surfaces (share, mouldboard) with used oil or grease and paint the frame.
Store under a roof, off the ground.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain why part P should be kept sharp.

points.description: A sharp share penetrates and cuts easily, so less draught is needed and the oxen tire less.
The plough stays in the ground at an even depth (a blunt share rides out).

explanation: Functions, adjustment and maintenance of the mouldboard plough.
hints: Name the part from its position, then its job.

stem: Thandeka grew 0.5 ha of groundnuts near Mutoko. She harvested 1,150 kg of dry pods, which gave 828 kg of kernels. Some pods stored in a damp shed went mouldy.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the yield of dry pods in t/ha.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the shelling percentage.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: When should gypsum be applied to the groundnuts?

options.content: Mixed with the seed at planting
options.rationale: Too early, and it is not a seed treatment.

options.content: At early flowering, over the rows
options.rationale: Correct: calcium is then in the pegging zone.

options.content: After the pods have been lifted
options.rationale: Too late to help pod filling.

options.content: Only to the following maize crop

parts.explanation: Pods absorb calcium directly from the soil around them as they fill.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Name the poison that can be produced by the mould on damp groundnuts.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain how the groundnuts should have been dried and stored to prevent mould.

points.description: Dry quickly with pods upwards, off damp soil, then in airy stacks until the pods rattle.
Store dry, in the shell, in a well-ventilated store off the floor.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Explain why groundnuts need little nitrogen fertiliser.

points.description: These fix nitrogen from the air for the plant.

explanation: Groundnut yield and shelling calculations, gypsum, aflatoxin and nitrogen fixation.
